- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially 1.00 or 0.50) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is neutral or negative (0.00) — add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Avoid over-optimistic 30-day forecasts after 18-day price consolidation — cap forecast rise to 3–5% above recent 18-day average.
- If sentiment history shows a recent 0.00 trend, forecast should not overshoot 10% above prior 3-day high — apply lag correction.
- When true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >10% under), check if sentiment was neutral — if so, adjust downward by 2–4% to avoid mean reversion bias.
- If forecast spikes after a 18-day downtrend, reduce forecast by 5–8% to avoid overreaction to short-term noise.
- For 30-day forecasts with sentiment history containing 0.50 or 1.00, apply a 3–5% downward bias to prevent overconfidence in sentiment-driven momentum.
